Troy Ounce vs Regular Ounce

A troy ounce is 31.1035 grams and is used only for precious metals. A regular ounce (avoirdupois), used for food and post, is 28.3495 grams. So a troy ounce is about 9.7% heavier. Confusing the two is a common and expensive mistake when buying gold or silver online.

Bullion coins and bars are sold in troy ounces: a 1 oz gold coin holds 31.1 grams of gold, and a 1 kilogram bar holds 32.15 troy ounces.

Questions & Answers

How many grams are in a troy ounce?

One troy ounce is exactly 31.1034768 grams, usually rounded to 31.1 grams.

Is a troy ounce the same as a regular ounce?

No. A regular (avoirdupois) ounce, used for food and parcels, is 28.35 grams. A troy ounce is about 10% heavier at 31.10 grams and is used only for gold, silver, platinum and other precious metals.

How many troy ounces are in a kilogram?

One kilogram is 32.1507 troy ounces. A standard 1 kg gold bar therefore holds just over 32 troy ounces.

Why are precious metals weighed in troy ounces?

The troy system dates back to medieval trade fairs in Troyes, France, and became the standard for bullion in London. Every international gold and silver price is still quoted per troy ounce.
